what_was_done: _leader_begun_near's ps probe runs with env={**os.environ, 'LC_ALL': 'C'}, so the birth stamp is always the C-locale 'Tue Nov 24 18:27:07 2026' whatever locale the caller's environment carries; the fixed-format strptime now always agrees with it (the plugin calls setlocale nowhere, verified by grep, so its own parsing stays C-locale). Tests: test_leader_begun_near_reads_a_localised_ps and test_lost_worker_restarts_once_under_a_localised_ps, each parametrized over en_GB.UTF-8 and de_DE.UTF-8 and skipped when `locale -a` does not list the locale. The first asserts _leader_begun_near(fresh_group, _now()) is True under the locale; the second runs the full lost-worker scenario (factored into _restart_after_lost_worker, shared with the unchanged test_lost_worker_restarts_once) under the locale and asserts the restart kills the orphaned command group. With the LC_ALL pin removed from the ps call, all four fail - _leader_begun_near answers False (en_GB prints 'Tue 24 Nov ...', de_DE 'Di. 24 Nov. ...') and the lost-worker test fails with 'the orphaned command group survived the restart', the form the finding describes; with the fix all pass.

env.start now decides on a record read after the lock probe in every branch: the read moved inside the probe branches, so the failed probe is followed by a read, never preceded by one. _held_answer's running branch re-reads the record before answering or replacing, and a running record whose pid is gone while the product lock is held is treated as a start in flight: the new _wait_for_running polls for the running record the holder will write (answering it at the same commit, replacing its product at another one) and never answers from the dead pid or stops on it; on timeout it returns the settling error. A new _pid_alive helper in jobs.py (os.kill(pid, 0)) backs the check. commands/env-start.md states the design side in one sentence: each start decides after its probe, and a held lock over a gone product is a start in flight. Tests: test_held_answer_answers_the_live_record_over_a_dead_pid_snapshot (stale running snapshot at the head commit over a live product: the answer carries the live pid, the product survives), test_held_answer_does_not_stop_on_a_stale_other_commit_snapshot (stale snapshot at another commit: the live record is answered, the product not stopped), and the pair test_overlapping_starts_agree_over_a_stale_record_at_the_head_commit / _at_another_commit, in which a stale running record (dead pid 999999) sits under a held product lock and two overlapping starts both return 0 with the same live pid. Against the pre-fix code all four fail (the dead pid answered, or the healthy product stopped, or the second start errored/started a second product), with every pre-existing test still passing; with the fix all 27 of test_env.py pass.
